# Pin the OH build inputs and distinguish analysis, packaging and execution

## Platform difference

A passing analyzer or an uploaded HAP artifact does not establish a signed, installable, feature-tested OH application.

## Implementation

SSH Codex pins an OH toolchain, generates its host and publishes an explicitly unsigned arm64 HAP. KikoFlu checks exact CLI/SDK API-release metadata. Bugaoshan uses marker directories for analysis but keeps a separate self-hosted real-SDK HAP job. MR allows unsigned artifact upload even when a preceding build result fails. Minecraft Box deletes its experimental analysis workflow; Zhiji explicitly reports build-only status separately from execution.

## Applicability

Preserve the distinction between workflow source, an observed CI run, native packaging, signing, installation and functional execution. The backfill contains source evidence only.

These observations apply to the pinned project revisions below, studied on 2026-09-30 and backfilled on 2026-10-06. Unspecified SDK/device compatibility remains unknown; this is not a fresh upstream assessment.

## Pitfalls and limitations

Empty SDK markers do not provide a native compiler. A deleted workflow no longer verifies anything. Commit subjects claiming builds completed can describe unrelated diffs; check actual workflow artifacts and results.

## Verification

Reproduce with pinned tools, inspect native build exit status and HAP identity/signature, then install and exercise features on target hardware. Record each completed tier separately.

Evidence tier: historical source/diff studies, with commit and path existence rechecked in local Git during this backfill. No application build, dependency resolution, signing, installation or device execution was performed. Proposed checks above are acceptance criteria, not completed tests.
